subject.title: Native hook relay starves mid-turn after long model-thinking gap (renewal loop tool-call-driven)

question: Should Codex native-hook relay recovery transparently refresh/rebind a missing or stale relay during an active turn, and under exactly which policy states may that recovery proceed without weakening PreToolUse enforcement?
rationale: The reported user-visible failure is a reliability bug, but the proposed retry/self-healing behavior crosses the native tool-approval boundary; source evidence must distinguish harmless no-policy recovery from required policy enforcement.

options.title: Require fail-closed self-healing proof
options.body: Implement refresh or re-registration only with a current-main regression that proves stale active-turn relays recover while required PreToolUse policy still blocks disallowed actions.

options.title: Keep fail-closed behavior pending diagnosis
options.body: Defer recovery behavior until the exact lifecycle failure is reproduced and classified, while keeping diagnostics and narrow race fixes separate.

options.title: Adopt an explicit opt-out path
options.body: Accept a documented configuration escape hatch for relay-only behavior while preserving required policy and approval relays, then track automatic recovery separately.

recommendation.title: Require fail-closed self-healing proof
recommendation.body: Implement refresh or re-registration only with a current-main regression that proves stale active-turn relays recover while required PreToolUse policy still blocks disallowed actions.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged reliability work scoped the adjacent bridge-record fix and is closest to the required safety-versus-recovery decision.
